expectations.text: The review flags SQL injection risk in the new route's query, specifically the use of sql.raw() with unsanitized user input, at or above high/critical severity.
expectations.evidence: outputs/findings.md, Finding 1 (graded Critical): "sql.raw(...) concatenates the unbounded q param straight into raw SQL — the one drizzle escape hatch that bypasses parameter binding. Noted a safe tagged-template alternative already used one file over, in context/repository.ts."

expectations.text: The review flags the missing workspace/tenant scoping on the PR lookup (broken access control / IDOR) at or above high/critical severity.
expectations.evidence: outputs/findings.md, Finding 3 (graded High): "No workspace filter on the PR lookup, unlike every sibling handler in the same file (GET /pulls/:id, resolvePrAndRepo) — cross-workspace PR search once there's more than one workspace."

expectations.text: The review flags that the GitHub token is being written to the application log in the error handler.
expectations.evidence: outputs/findings.md, Finding 2 (graded Critical): "The catch block fetches the live GITHUB_TOKEN and logs it in plaintext — trivial to trigger, since a single stray quote in q already breaks the injected SQL and lands here."

claims.claim: A safe tagged-template alternative to sql.raw already exists elsewhere in the codebase (context/repository.ts)
claims.evidence: Cited by file path in the review; consistent with drizzle-orm's documented sql`` tagged-template parameterization, which the reviewer contrasted with the unsafe sql.raw() used in the fixture.

eval_feedback.overall: No suggestions — this run genuinely found all three planted issues with correct severity and concrete, checkable evidence, not by coincidence. The two unplanted extras (unvalidated q param, growing the routes.ts db-access debt) are real and additive, not noise.
